summary: Today's decision holds up on the information available. I took the Market Analyst's risk-off stance, made one small buy (SAM, $15, filled at $220.142), sold nothing, left cash near 11.4%, and wrote three thesis_updates (re-dating the SPY 200-day for VOO and VTI, giving VTI's cost clause a dollar level, and making MCO's text match its $470 stop). The account fell $5.58 (about -0.89%) to $620.78. Over the same day the SPY benchmark fell about 1.02% and the shadow about 1.24%, and since the 11-10 version the account is -0.28% against SPY -2.33%. That is one day and proves nothing about the calls. No price stop tripped and no qualitative clause tripped on the inputs I have. SAM closed at $224.68, +2.06% on its fill and +0.62% on the day. Three things matter for tomorrow. (1) VOO and VTI are both NEAR: SPY marks 732.44 against the shared 729.58 stop, +0.39% per the stop block, and Nvidia reports tonight. One close below the 200-day line the regime filter computes would trip about 23.4% of equity in one go (VOO 13.4% plus VTI 10.0%). Holding cash above the buffer instead of adding to US core was the right side of that risk. (2) MCO and MSCI fell together (-4.32% and -4.20%), so the financial-data sleeve moved as one position. MCO is now only +3.07% above its $470 stop per its stop block, the closest single-stock stop. The sleeve is about 8.1% of equity. (3) SAM's stored invalidation still measures the $201 stop from the $223.29 menu close. I knowingly left it that way because the fill was not yet known (L6 permits this), but it has to be restated from the $220.142 fill at the next run. Against the fill, $201 is about 8.7% away, not the roughly 10% I accepted from the Skeptic for SAM's 0.383 vol. The decision's weakest point is timing. I bought into the Staples bucket two sessions before WMT's 11-19 print and departed in part from my own 11-13 'wait for the prints' line. I said so explicitly and kept the size at $15, which is how the departure should be handled. I still cannot judge it before 11-19.
lessons: Next run, restate SAM's stop from the $220.142 fill through thesis_updates (L6). Use about $198 (10% under the fill) to keep the vol-based width I accepted from the Skeptic. If $201 stays, the text must say it is about 8.7% under the fill. The text must not keep referring to the menu close.

VOO/VTI pre-commitment (L9): if tomorrow's stop block shows the shared SPY stop tripped, sell VOO and VTI together as one position. Do not re-date the moving 200-day figure in a way that moves the line out of reach after a breach. Re-dating is only for keeping the stored number current, not for avoiding a trip.

MCO and MSCI fell about 4.3% together on a day when Financials was a favored sector. Treat them as one sleeve with two stops: no adds to either until MCO is comfortably clear of $470. If MCO trips, re-check MSCI's case the same run rather than assuming the sleeve's thesis survives. One day is not evidence, but it confirms the L3 overlap reading.

When I depart from an earlier stated commitment (here the 11-13 'deploy after the Nvidia and WMT prints'), naming the departure and keeping the size small was the right way to handle it. The post-11-19 deployment commitment still stands, conditional on the regime filter holding. If SPY closes below its 200-day, the cash above the buffer should wait for a new reason rather than go into equities by default.
